topic: What trade-offs exist between array size and radiation efficiency for SIW arrays in high-gain inter-satellite antennas?
consensus_response: Increasing array size in SIW arrays for high-gain inter-satellite antennas leads to a trade-off between directivity and radiation efficiency. Larger arrays provide better directivity but result in higher insertion loss due to longer structures, reducing realized gain from 70% to 27.5%. Surface roughness exacerbates this issue, especially at higher frequencies, introducing additional insertion loss. Hybrid SIW waveguide power dividers can mitigate coupling effects and maintain performance in large arrays. Design optimization techniques, such as genetic algorithms or simulated annealing, can help minimize insertion loss by optimizing element spacing and material selection.
reference_context: The reference context provides factual ground-truth on the relationship between array scale and efficiency, with a 16x16 SIW sub-array exhibiting a drastic drop in radiation efficiency from 70% to 27.5% as the array size increases.
